name: repeated login failures from a host the account does not own
rationale: S3 counts authentication failures inside a thirty second window. The 27 training variants spread 3 to 5 failures over up to 21.4 hours, so the burst never forms and the signal never fires. Counting the same failures per 24h and only from a host the account does not own keeps the claim and drops the timing assumption. The benign sample's worst run of failures from a host the account does not own is 0, so the threshold is set at 3.
when: ip_owner != $u AND count(status=401, user=$u, ip=$ip, window=24h) >= 3
explain: {user} failed to authenticate {count} times from {ip} within 24 hours, and that host does not belong to the account.

real_incident.explanation: sarah_j failed to authenticate 3 times from 10.0.8.45 within 24 hours, and that host does not belong to the account.

name: csrf payload in a forum parameter
rationale: The payload parameters on /intranet/forum/new in the real incident are action, payload, script, and 2 of those lines carry the string 'csrf' in the value. Matching on it reproduces the March incident exactly. Whether it detects anything else depends on whether the attacker's choice of word is part of the attack, which is what the held-out check is for.
explain: {user} posted to {template} from {ip} with a parameter containing csrf.

gate.rejected_reason: Held-out detection 0.00 against a threshold of 0.60. The rule fired on 0 of 40 variants generated from seeds and personas it never saw. It catches the incident it was written from and not the attack behind it.

real_incident.explanation: david_m posted to /intranet/forum/new from 10.0.8.45 with a parameter containing csrf.
